projects.title: Page Blocks — Composable Content Engine
projects.subtitle: The block-based page system behind Creation.com — and the one rendering this site
projects.summary: A Directus many-to-any block system where editors compose pages from a library of reusable block types, rendered by a dynamic Vue component map — with click-to-edit visual editing on the live site.
projects.featured: M2A architecture · visual editing · powers this site
projects.problem: Every layout change on Creation.com used to need a developer. The editorial team wanted to compose, reorder, and publish rich pages — sections, galleries, FAQs, testimonials, products, video series — without touching code, and without the design system fragmenting into one-off page builds.

architecture.text: A `page` collection and a `page_blocks` many-to-any junction (collection / item / sort) let one page own an ordered mix of block types, where each block type is its own Directus collection with exactly the fields it needs.
A dynamic renderer on the Nuxt side maps block types to Vue components, so a page is data all the way down — adding a new block type means one new collection and one new component.
Directus visual editing overlays click-to-edit controls on the live site, so editors adjust blocks in place — the 'visual editor'.
The block library grew to cover page sections, galleries, FAQs, testimonials, people, products, and video series, all reusable across the site.

This portfolio implements the same architecture in miniature: the homepage is a `page` row composed of `page_blocks` rows, authored in a local Dockerized Directus and snapshotted into the repo at build time.

outcomes.text: The editorial team composes and publishes complete pages with zero developer involvement.
New landing pages ship in minutes instead of going through a development cycle.
Page structure became data with a single source of truth, replacing hardcoded layouts.
The pattern was designed once and now renders everything from campaign pages to this portfolio.

projects.callout: You're looking at it: this site's homepage is rendered by a simplified version of this exact system — a Directus `page` row composed of `page_blocks`, with visual editing in dev. The repo shows the whole pattern end to end.

projects.title: Cross-Channel Analytics Hub
projects.subtitle: Unified sales, email, and social metrics for leadership across 7 offices
projects.summary: A pluggable adapter system that syncs metrics from 7 e-commerce stores and 5 marketing channels into unified, permission-scoped dashboards.
projects.problem: Leadership across 7 international offices had no single view of performance. Sales lived in 7 regional PrestaShop stores (each in its own currency), email metrics in GetResponse across 17 mailing lists, and social reach across YouTube, Facebook, and Instagram. Reporting meant manually pulling numbers from five different admin panels.

architecture.text: Designed a pluggable adapter system: each channel (PrestaShop, GetResponse, YouTube, Facebook, Instagram) implements a common sync interface, so adding a new source is a new adapter — not a rewrite.
Nightly automated syncs plus on-demand backfills, with per-store currency handling for the 7 international PrestaShop instances.
Normalized metrics into Directus collections that power dashboard queries.
Vue 3 + ApexCharts dashboards with cross-channel KPIs, period-over-period deltas, and per-channel deep dives.
Office-scoped row-level access policies so each office sees exactly its own data — leadership sees the whole picture.

outcomes.text: One permission-scoped dashboard replaced five separate admin panels for reporting.
Leadership across 7 offices reviews unified, always-current KPIs instead of hand-built spreadsheets.
New channels can be onboarded by writing a single adapter against the sync interface.

projects.title: Contacts Database (CRM)
projects.subtitle: The organization-wide system of record on Directus
projects.summary: A 26-collection Directus CRM managing contacts, subscriber lists, and digital-content access across 7 international offices — replacing a legacy dual-write system.
projects.featured: 26 collections · 7 offices · sole system of record
projects.problem: Customer data was split across a legacy system and newer tools, kept in sync by fragile dual writes. There was no single source of truth for who a contact was, what they subscribed to, or what digital content they could access.

architecture.text: Designed a 26-collection Directus schema covering contacts, subscriber lists, and digital-content access, built in collaboration with a senior developer.
Modeled office-level data ownership with row-level access policies across 7 international offices.
Migrated off the legacy dual-write system so the CRM became the sole system of record.
Integrated with the email platform (GetResponse list sync, batch uploads, bulk unsubscribe) via custom Directus extensions.

outcomes.text: Eliminated dual-write drift: one system of record for contacts, subscriptions, and content access.
Non-technical staff in every office manage customer data through Directus with scoped permissions.
Became the foundation the analytics hub and email platform are built on.

projects.title: WARP — Creation.com Redesign
projects.subtitle: Full redesign and migration of a site with millions of monthly visitors
projects.summary: Migrated a legacy site to Nuxt 3 + Directus on a fully headless architecture — preserving SEO rankings and uptime throughout.
projects.featured: Millions of monthly visitors · zero SEO regression
projects.problem: Creation.com ran on a legacy stack that made content changes slow and developer-dependent, and its architecture limited performance. The migration had to happen without losing search rankings or uptime for a site serving millions of monthly visitors.

architecture.text: Rebuilt the site on Nuxt 3 with Directus as a fully headless CMS.
Powered content pages with the page-block composable content engine (its own case study), so the editorial team composes and publishes pages without developer involvement.
Optimized page-load performance with SSR, asset optimization, and Cloudflare-backed delivery.
Managed the migration with redirect mapping and metadata parity to preserve SEO rankings and uptime continuity.

outcomes.text: Improved page-load performance on a fully headless architecture.
Editorial team builds and publishes landing pages independently — no developer bottleneck.
SEO rankings and uptime held steady through the entire migration.

projects.title: The Creation Daily — Email Delivery Platform
projects.subtitle: End-to-end transactional and marketing email at 100K+ daily sends
projects.summary: A full-stack email system integrating Nuxt frontend forms, Directus backend workflows, GetResponse, and dynamic MJML + Liquid.js templating.
projects.problem: The organization needed to reliably reach 100K+ daily subscribers with both transactional and marketing email — with personalized content, manageable templates, and subscriber lists that stay in sync with the CRM.

architecture.text: Nuxt frontend forms feeding Directus backend workflows for signups, preferences, and unsubscribes.
MJML templating compiled to responsive email HTML, with Liquid.js for dynamic per-recipient personalization.
GetResponse integration managing 17 mailing lists, send schedules, and delivery logs.
Directus workflows as the operational layer: staff manage lists, schedules, and content without touching code.

outcomes.text: Supports 100K+ daily sends across transactional and marketing email.
Template changes are compiled MJML — consistent rendering across email clients.
Subscriber lists stay consistent with the CRM system of record.

projects.title: AI Receipt Export Tool
projects.subtitle: An AI OCR pipeline that eliminated manual travel-expense transcription
projects.summary: Speakers upload trip receipts, an AI OCR pipeline extracts line-item data, staff review in an editing UI, and one click exports to Excel or the CRM.
projects.featured: AI OCR · human-in-the-loop review · one-click export
projects.problem: Returning speakers submitted stacks of paper travel receipts that staff transcribed into spreadsheets by hand — slow, error-prone, and entirely manual.

architecture.text: Upload flow where speakers submit trip receipts from any device.
AI OCR pipeline extracts line-item data (vendor, date, amounts, categories) from receipt images.
Human-in-the-loop review UI where staff verify and correct extracted data before it goes anywhere.
One-click export to Excel or directly into the Directus contacts database.
The same AI-tooling pattern (extract → review → export) was reused to accelerate processes in other departments.

outcomes.text: Replaced fully manual expense transcription with an automated, reviewable pipeline.
Staff time shifted from data entry to quick verification.
Established a reusable AI-tooling pattern adopted by other departments.

projects.title: Commenting System — Migration & Moderation UX
projects.subtitle: Legacy comment migration plus a purpose-built reply experience for authors
projects.summary: Migrated two legacy commenting systems into the Directus platform and rebuilt moderation end-to-end — a custom reply interface, publish-and-notify flows, and help-desk-synced spam banning.
projects.featured: legacy migration · custom reply UI · anti-spam sync
projects.problem: Comments on Creation.com ran on a legacy system that was never fully fleshed out. Reader comments were only loosely hooked into the new site, and authors replied to commenters through a fragile general-purpose popup stack that broke under platform upgrades, silently dropped empty replies, and previewed commenter-submitted HTML unsafely. Moderation roles existed on paper but couldn't actually manage comments, and spam handling was entirely manual.

architecture.text: Migrated comments from two legacy platforms into a single Directus comment collection serving the Nuxt frontend, filtering purged content during import so removed comments never resurfaced.

Designed and shipped a purpose-built comment-reply Directus interface (its own extension package): from the notification e-mail an author lands on the comment and gets a Compose Reply dialog with rich text, reason selection, and inline confirmation — structured so the stacked-dialog focus-trap failure that plagued the old popup cannot recur by construction.
Reply actions trigger Directus flows with explicit payloads — publish-with-response and private e-mail — and reply e-mails preserve the author’s formatting.
Hardened by default: commenter HTML renders as inert plain text in previews (no XSS path), and an empty-reply guard stops the flow from dying silently.
Fixed the Comment Manager role so moderation permissions actually work, and added bidirectional ban sync between the comment system and the help desk’s spam rules.

outcomes.text: Authors and editors reply to commenters from one friendly dialog — publish with a response, or answer privately by e-mail — instead of wrestling a breaking popup.
Years of legacy comments consolidated onto the new platform, with purged content filtered out during migration.
Moderation is safer and faster: inert previews, working role permissions, and spam bans that sync both ways with the help desk.

item.heading: Full-stack, end to end
item.body:
For nearly three years I've been the full-stack developer behind Creation.com and its surrounding platform: a Directus-based CRM spanning 7 international offices, a cross-channel analytics hub, an email delivery platform reaching 100K+ subscribers daily, and a growing set of AI-powered internal tools.

I specialize in owning systems end-to-end — database design, API architecture, background sync pipelines, responsive frontends, and the CMS integrations that let non-technical teams run them.

item.heading: Case studies from production
item.intro: Seven systems I designed and shipped — each case study covers the problem, the architecture, and what it changed.
item.more_text: Tour booking and conference registration systems, an expense-forms platform, teleprompter automation for the production team, Google Apps Script workflows, and a growing set of AI/MCP integrations. Happy to walk through any of them.
